alignment_method: hybrid: tfidf shortlist -> grade+keyword rerank -> LLM curation (Claude Sonnet)
notes: High-school 4-paragraph argumentative essay on the consequences of Romeo and Juliet's actions.

objectives.title: Essay Header
objectives.note: Logistical formatting. No ELA standard applies.

objectives.title: Essay Title
objectives.description: Title your essay (assigned title: 'Romeo and Juliet Consequences Essay').

alignments.rationale: Task-appropriate writing convention; but the prescribed title leaves little author discretion.

objectives.title: Essay Sections
objectives.description: Insert Section Break (continuous) so GradeFlow can identify sections.
objectives.note: Platform-specific document structure. No ELA standard applies.

objectives.title: Introduction Paragraph
objectives.description: Follow Introduction Paragraph requirements in the instructions.

alignments.rationale: Introduce precise claim(s) and establish clear relationships among claim(s), reasons, and evidence.
Write arguments to support claims — the overall argument-writing standard.

objectives.title: Hook and Thesis Statement
objectives.description: Write a powerful hook and a clear thesis statement.

alignments.rationale: Introduce a precise claim — the thesis itself — and hook the reader into the argument's framing.

objectives.title: First Body Paragraph
objectives.description: Topic sentence, two quotes, commentary linking to thesis.

alignments.rationale: Develop claim(s) fairly, supplying evidence for each.
Cite strong and thorough textual evidence from Shakespeare's play to support analysis.

objectives.title: Second Body Paragraph
objectives.description: Topic sentence, two quotes, commentary (as in first body paragraph).

alignments.rationale: Develop claims with evidence.
Cite textual evidence from the play.

objectives.title: Body Paragraph Evidence
objectives.description: Verify both body paragraphs are in correct sections and have required structure.

alignments.rationale: Quality of evidence/development within each body paragraph.
Linking words/phrases that clarify relationships between claims, reasons, and evidence.

objectives.title: Conclusion Paragraph
objectives.description: Restate thesis in new words, summarize points, leave final impression.

alignments.rationale: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument.

objectives.title: Intro Paragraph (Teacher Review)
objectives.description: Hook, background (title/author), summary, thesis — graded by teacher.

alignments.rationale: Intro + thesis framing — core of the argument introduction.

objectives.title: Body Paragraph #1 (Teacher Review — evidence)
objectives.description: Two well-chosen quotes, each properly introduced.

alignments.rationale: Evidence selection and integration graded here.
Citation of strong textual evidence from the play.

objectives.title: Body Paragraph #1 Commentary
objectives.description: Two pieces of analysis per quote explaining its support of the thesis.

alignments.rationale: Developing claims with reasoning — the commentary-on-evidence work.
Determine a theme or central idea and analyze in detail its development — what commentary ties back to.

objectives.title: Body Paragraph #2 (Teacher Review — evidence)
objectives.description: Same criteria as body #1: two well-chosen quotes properly introduced.

alignments.rationale: Evidence selection and integration.
Citation of textual evidence.

objectives.title: Body Paragraph #2 Commentary
objectives.description: Analysis per quote explaining thesis support.

alignments.rationale: Developing claims with reasoning.
Analyzing theme development through commentary.

objectives.title: V4 Conclusion Paragraph
objectives.description: Restate thesis, summarize, explain overall message/lesson.

alignments.rationale: Provide a concluding statement or section that follows from and supports the argument.

objectives.title: Overall Structure / Format
objectives.description: MLA format, correct grammar, varied sentence structure.

alignments.rationale: Conventions of standard English grammar and usage.
Capitalization, punctuation, and spelling.
Apply knowledge of language — vary sentence structure for effect.
Produce clear, coherent writing appropriate to task and purpose.
